scope: Independent complete source/test review and fresh isolated MSVC execution of the STATUS wrapper component.
result: No blocking finding in the bounded wrapper contract.
checks: Pool offsets agree with the recorded 80 by 632-byte pool and following free-list/count. Init admits free startup slots; reset checks pool identity independently of old free-list contents.
Every bound original forwards once outside the SRW lock. Native SEH crosses the wrapper unchanged and finally drains the ticket while faulting confidence.
Cross-thread overlapping originals block metadata transactions; per-thread nesting and independent cross-thread return order are exercised.
Arguments retain pointer width and signed coefficient values; full integer returns and incoming/outgoing LastError are preserved.
A transaction can validate pool, compare revisions/bits, invalidate a manual write and mutate inside one lock. The trusted callback must not reenter, wait for a native callback, or invoke originals.
Invalid pool observations and transaction SEH lose confidence. No claim is made that a destroyed Observer object or arbitrary observer-memory corruption can preserve native forwarding.
Bootstrap is distinct from Observing; the API does not infer an external barrier from an empty tracked-call count.
remaining: Actor/status binding and typed ownership/transport receipts
